overall: The AG found the School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law when its Chair surveyed members outside a noticed meeting on whether to create an audit oversight subcommittee, rejecting the claim that this was administrative scheduling; ordered future compliance and reconstructed minutes within 30 days.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee deliberated outside a noticed meeting when the Chair polled members on whether to create a special education audit oversight subcommittee.
allegations.key_passage: Here, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law when the Chair surveyed members outside of a noticed meeting to determine whether the Committee wished to consider creating an audit oversight subcommittee, and collectively the Committee decided to take no action toward creating such a subcommittee.

allegations.summary: Complaint noted the special education audit was discussed at two meetings without being listed on the notice; the AG read the complaint as really about outside deliberation, so it was not separately decided.
allegations.key_passage: based on the complaint as a whole and the request for further review, we understand the thrust of the complaint to be that the Committee deliberated outside of a meeting regarding whether to create a subcommittee.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
Within 30 days of receipt of the letter, create meeting minutes capturing the discussions held and decisions made through the communications at issue, using notes and member recollections as needed.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law’s requirements and note that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law. Additionally, we order the Committee, within 30 days of receipt of this letter, to create meeting minutes capturing the discussions held and decisions made through the communications at issue in this determination.
